brief: Studies one fragment inside a text: where it occurs, how often, what the text becomes without it, and how it sits among other fragments.
detail: Built with a fragment, a text and a flag that says whether comparisons respect case (1) or ignore it (0); stzStringSubString is the same class with the flag fixed at 1. Nothing here changes either text: the Replaced, Removed, Uppercased and Lowercased forms return a new text. Positions count characters, so Hebrew, Arabic and emoji text is located where you expect. Found today: Positions and Occurrences raise R14 because they call a finder method that does not exist; NumberOfOccurrence and Replaced do not count overlapping occurrences while Sections and NthPosition do; and IsBoundedBy compares the enclosed stretch with the fragment exactly, so the flag 0 does not reach that last step.
